verdict.rationale: Buzz's own Desktop-bundled managed agent takes natural-language requests in channels. It ships a vendor skill that maps conversational asks onto relay operations: messaging, channels, DMs, workflows, repos, canvas, memory and agent creation. Users steer agents by @mentioning them, and Block keeps a benchmark that grades how agents answer ordinary-looking questions through Buzz, such as creating channels and inviting users. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language operation works reliably, and evidence that admin, moderation and deployment operations can also be driven conversationally (agent creation goes through an owner-review form rather than completing from the command alone).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: When someone naturally asks to create an agent, ask for at most two things: the agent's name and what it should do day-to-day
relay operations: owner-reviewed agent drafts, messaging, channels, DMs, users, workflows, feed, reactions, canvas, social, repos, uploads, and agent memory.
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
you mention it to steer it, you tell a healthy agent to stop and it exits on its own.
